solves.reason: (A) gathered: crowds came together. (B) refugee: person fleeing Naples. (C) cease: hostilities would stop.
(A) dared: hardly dared believe. (B) confirmed: he verified the news. (C) joy: cried with joy.
(A) dispatch: military term for sent rider. (B) armistice: peace agreement signed. (C) overflow: joy overflowed from heart.
refused doesn't fit. Original is dared - she hardly dared believe, not refused.
questioned doesn't fit. He confirmed (not questioned) the armistice.
pulling into is wrong. The rider was pulling OUT OF the castle, not into it.
Hostilities would cease (stop). returned/gathered/shouting make no sense with Hostilities as subject.
He confirmed the armistice. heard/shouting/waved describe others' actions.
Joy seemed to overflow from her heart. cease/returned/gathered don't fit with joy + from her heart.
refugee ≈ exile. Both mean someone forced from their homeland.
cease ≈ stop. Both mean to end/halt.
dispatch ≈ sent. A dispatch rider is one sent to deliver messages.
gathered ↔ dispersed. To gather is opposite of to disperse.
overflow ↔ drain. To overflow is opposite of to drain away.
(A) confirm = verify truth. (B) confirm in church = religious confirmation/견진.
Person forced to leave country to escape war = refugee.
had been + past participle = passive voice past perfect.
Participial phrase: Hurrying back... they heard. Present participle for simultaneous action.
until she heard it with her own ears. She needed personal confirmation.
waved him down = flagged the rider to stop. Context: they wanted to confirm the news.
